requirement:
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
rationale:
The two marked tests in `src/authoring/tools.rs` cover the obligations in `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.excerpts`. I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not read the implementation.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. Every `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text, is clipped to the span of the item named by `file` and `item`.
2. The span includes the item's attached source: comments and attributes, under `requirements.references.outline_comments`.
3. Clipping applies within a line that several items share.

**Coverage in `search_excerpts_stop_at_byte_boundaries_including_attached_comments_and_attributes`**
- **Both tools:** the test runs `ripgrep` with `context: 99` and `ast_grep` with a Rust rule, and checks the same invariants for each.
- **Own-line neighbours and context:** the source puts `fn before` and `fn after` on their own lines around `fn target`, and a `fn last` after the shared line. With context 99, any leaked context line would show up. The test asserts that `unwanted_before`, `unwanted_after`, `unwanted_last` and `fn last` never appear anywhere in the result.
- **Shared line:** `fn left() {…} /* needle attached */ #[inline] fn right() {…} fn last() {…}` puts three items on one line. The test asserts these results:
  - There are exactly three matches, with items `fn[target]`, `fn[left]` and `fn[right]`.
  - The `fn[left]` excerpt does not contain `fn right`.
  - The `fn[right]` excerpt does not contain `fn left`.
  - The `fn[right]` excerpt does not contain `needle attached`.
  - The `fn[left]` excerpt does contain `needle attached`. The comment follows other source on its line, so it belongs to the innermost item containing that line.
  - The `fn[right]` excerpt contains `#[inline] fn right`, which is its attached attribute.
  - `fn last` never appears, so clipping holds on the right edge of the shared line as well as the left.
- **Attached source on the target:** for `ripgrep`, the `fn[target]` excerpt must contain `needle docs` (the doc comment) and `#[inline]`. It must also contain `café`, which exercises multi-byte text at the clipping boundaries. A separate query for `inline` with `context: 0` confirms the attribute lines are attributed to `src/lib.rs#fn[target]` and `src/lib.rs#fn[right]`.
- **Redaction alongside clipping:** the token is absent and `[REDACTED:` is present.
- **Narrow query:** a query for `café` with `context: 0` yields one match, in `fn[target]`.

**Coverage in `exact_match_ranges_preserve_regex_anchors_and_skip_unmatched_or_binary_sources`**
- With `context: 10` and anchored or case-insensitive patterns, the test asserts that the excerpt is exactly `fn exact() { needle(); }` with `matched: true`.
- Neither the following line `fn last() {}` nor any other text leaks into the excerpt. The assertion is an exact equality on the lines array.
- Broken and binary sources produce no excerpts.

**Gaps considered and rejected**
- Languages other than Rust are not tested, but the requirement states the clipping rule generically. The Rust test exercises both a comment and an attribute as attached source.
- `ast_grep` has no context parameter, and its matched lines are checked on the shared-line case.

I found no unresolved ambiguity and no acknowledged gaps (the acknowledgments list is empty).

text: :::{req} search_accounting.excerpts
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
